title: Strong randomized verification implies BPP
statement: Let $E$ be a verifier model, let $d$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $L$ be a language of bit strings. If there is an $E$-efficient randomized verifier using a polynomially bounded number of random bits such that, on inputs of length $n$, it accepts members and rejects nonmembers with probability at least $1-2^{-((n+1)^d+1)}$, then $L$ has an $E$-efficient randomized verifier with both correctness probabilities at least $2/3$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ has an $E$-efficient verifier with polynomially bounded randomness and correctness probability at least $1-2^{-((n+1)^d+1)}$ on inputs of length $n$
